summary: Brandywine's 93-foot steel tower (1928) was announced in 1938 for a rebuild to 120 feet for radio; a 2007 state report says it later moved to Fairview in Clear Spring, MD.

facts.status_note: The original Brandywine site is listed as gone. The tower now stands at the Fairview Outdoor Education Center in Clear Spring, Washington County.
facts.agency: Maryland State Forestry Department, later managed by the Department of Natural Resources

access.note: On the grounds of a Washington County Public Schools outdoor school. The sources describe school programs and say nothing about public visits.

events.note: One of two steel observation towers erected in Maryland that year; this one 93 feet high at Brandywine, Prince George County.
February 1938 announcement that the 93-foot tower would be rebuilt to 120 feet to carry a two-way radio set. The article says the rebuild was under way; no completion date was found.

evidence.supports: Built in 1928 as one of two steel observation towers, this one 93 feet high at Brandywine
evidence.quote: Two steel observation towers were erected in Maryland in 1928, one 93 feet high at Brandywine, Prince George County.

evidence.supports: February 1938 announcement by the State Forestry Department
evidence.quote: Construction of a new radio-equipped fire tower at Brandy Wine, in Southern Maryland, was announced today by the State Forestry Department.

evidence.supports: Rebuild to 120 feet for two-way radio, under way in 1938
evidence.quote: the department was rebuilding a 93-foot tower to a height of 120 feet to give the two-way radio outfit greater range.

evidence.supports: Radio set to be built at the forestry radio laboratory in Laurel
evidence.quote: The set itself will be constructed in the forestry's radio laboratory at Laurel.

evidence.supports: Plan to extend radio service into Southern Maryland
evidence.quote: Quick said completion of the Brandy Wine station will mark the start of a program to extend forestry radio service into Southern Maryland.

evidence.supports: Property transferred to the University of Maryland
evidence.quote: Brandywine Forestry Tower. Property was transferred to the University of Maryland.

evidence.supports: Tower now at the Fairview Outdoor Education Center, Clear Spring, Washington County
evidence.quote: resides at the Fairview Outdoor Education Center, Clear Spring, Washington County, Maryland.

evidence.supports: Tower moved from its original location
evidence.quote: The following towers were moved from their original location and now reside at other sites.

evidence.supports: Original Brandywine site listed as gone
Article's author affiliation: Claud E. Kitchens Outdoor School listed under Washington County Public Schools
Tower came into the possession of Washington County Public Schools after decommissioning
evidence.quote: it somehow came into the possession of the Washington County Public School System

evidence.supports: Tower is 104 feet tall; students climb it at the Fairview school
evidence.quote: Ask any student who has visited the Claud E. Kitchens Outdoor School at Fairview in Clear Spring, MD for a favorite memory, and many will recount the climb up the 104-foot fire tower.

evidence.supports: Climb has been a rite of passage for Grade 5 students for about 40 years
evidence.quote: For 40 or so years it has been a rite of passage for thousands of local Grade 5 students.

evidence.supports: Article presents the tower as part of the school's teaching program
evidence.quote: My colleagues and I wanted to use this valuable resource to enrich student learning and support our Maryland State Learning Standards.

evidence.supports: Article says the tower was once active on Maryland's Eastern Shore (conflicting claim)
evidence.quote: This gem once existed as an active fire tower on Maryland’s Eastern Shore

corrections.current: None relocated (The lookout was moved to the Fairview Outdoor Center.)
corrections.proposed: relocated to the Fairview Outdoor Education Center, Clear Spring, Washington County (year not yet found)
corrections.why: The record's event text is not a valid event and uses a different name for the site. The state report names the Fairview Outdoor Education Center. A move date is needed before the event can be added.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 2022 teacher article says the Fairview tower was once active on Maryland's Eastern Shore. The 1938 article places Brandy Wine in Southern Maryland, and the state report links the Brandywine tower to Fairview. This record follows the state report and the 1938 article and treats the article's origin claim as unconfirmed.
Sources give 93 feet in 1928, 120 feet as the height the 1938 rebuild was planned to reach, and 104 feet for the Fairview tower in a 2022 article. The record's 28.3 m matches the 1928 height only.

sources.title: Brandywine (quoting The Forest Worker, March 1929, and The Daily Times, February 15, 1938)
Forestry Towers and Forestry Tower Properties (April 2007)
New Life for an Old Fire Tower

notes_for_editor: The 1928 and 1938 facts rest on newspaper quotes reproduced on a volunteer site, not on the original papers. No source gives the move date or the date of the University of Maryland transfer, so no relocated event is listed. No staffing or fire history was found, so none is written. Heights: 93 ft (1928), 120 ft (planned 1938 rebuild; completion not found), 104 ft (2022 article for Fairview). facts.height_m keeps the 1928 figure; decide whether the current height should replace it. The Eastern Shore origin claim and the 104-foot height conflict with the state report and the 1938 article and are unresolved. Access level 'restricted' is an editorial reading of a school site; confirm with Washington County Public Schools before publishing any visiting guidance. Lead, not used: a WCPS bid page for restoring the fire tower at the Claud E. Kitchens Outdoor School (https://wcpspurchasing.com/group/917/fire-tower-restoration-claud-e-kitchens-outdoor-school) appeared in search results only; it was not read and is undated. The brief's source_pages link ../us-md-brandywine-at-fairview-outdoor-center/ returns 404 and was not used. The state report is dated April 2007 and has no DRAFT label, so an earlier DRAFT tag was removed. Search budget used: 2 searches.
